# Session Handoff: Floor 2 generated industrial-cave terrain pack + render-fix wiring + crenellation fix

## Date

2026-07-24

## Persona

Producer → Sprite/Terrain Engineer (multi-layer: art generation + engine render wiring)

## Systems touched

sprite-pipeline, mapgen

## Apples

4🍎 estimated, 4🍎 actual (see docs/knowledge/metrics/apples/2026-07-24-floor2-industrial-cave-generated-art.json)

## What Was Done

Replaced the 100% procedural placeholder `industrial-cave` terrain pack with real
**Azure gpt-image-1-generated** art (materials generated by the hosted model, then
**composed locally over the existing blob47 wall silhouettes** so edge continuity is
preserved), fixed a **wall crenellation** bug in the shared compose geometry, and — the
big one — fixed the render wiring so Floor 2 **actually renders the pack**.

**Observed in the real `MainGameScene`** (via `main-scene-probe-lab`, which boots the real
scene headlessly and reads `terrainRenderSummary`) — before: **0 pack walls / 0 pack floors**
on the representative Floor 2 seed (pack silently fell through to the legacy tileset); after:
**11,509 pack walls + 28,291 pack floors**. Also confirmed visually in `npm run dev` (human
approved `files/floor2-pack-lit.png` + `files/floor2-tileset.png`).

Changes (committed `049100b4c`):

- **Render fix** — `src/engine/scenes/BootScene.ts` now calls `preloadTerrainPacks(this.load)`
  in `preload()`. This was **dead code** (nothing called it), so pack textures were never
  queued into a Phaser loader; the renderer's `scene.textures.exists(key)` guard then silently
  fell through to the legacy Floor-1 tileset. Phaser runs `preload()` before `create()`, so the
  textures are now resident before `MainGameScene` bakes the terrain layer.
- **Crenellation fix** — `scripts/sprites/terrain-packs/quadrant-kit.ts` uses a uniform inset
  rectangle (`WALL_INSET_PX=48`) instead of the per-quadrant carve that produced a
  battlement/crenellation top edge. A wall cell's **alpha channel IS the silhouette**, so this
  lives in the shared compose geometry.
- **Wiring chain** — `floor2.manifest.json` (`terrainPackId: "industrial-cave"`) →
  `floor-main-scene-options.ts` (forwards it) → `MainGameScene.ts` (threads into
  `buildTerrainLayer`, widens `terrainRenderSummary` with `packWallCount/packFloorCount/packCorridorCount`)
  → `main-scene-probe-lab/index.ts` (mirrors the widened interface).
- **Provenance honesty + build safety** — truthful `provenance` block in the committed manifest
  (`kind: "authored"`, author names the Azure model + local composition, note states the
  committed PNGs are the source of truth and are **not byte-reproducible**); env-guarded the
  procedural writer in `build-industrial-cave.ts` (`TERRAIN_PACKS_ALLOW_PROCEDURAL_OVERWRITE=1`)
  so a routine `terrain-packs:build` cannot clobber the shipped art.
- **Tests** — NEW `tests/unit/sprites/terrain-pack-committed.test.ts` validates the **committed**
  manifest + **shipped** PNGs on disk (the runtime source of truth via `terrain-pack-registry.ts`,
  which every prior test skipped by validating only the in-memory procedural builder): schema, 47
  masks, pool/door image existence+dims, atlas 512×384, **188/188 (100%) authored edge-compat**
  (durable crenellation-fix proof), and provenance honesty. Extended
  `boot-scene-generated-sprite-gate.test.ts` with a source-assertion guard that `preload()` calls
  `preloadTerrainPacks`. `floor-manifest-terrain-pack.test.ts` asserts Floor 2 → industrial-cave.

## Key Decisions Made

- **Committed PNGs are the source of truth, not a byte-reproducible build.** Generation is a
  hosted model + local composition; forcing a deterministic builder would either re-introduce
  placeholder art or misrepresent reproducibility. Kept the procedural builder as a validated
  fallback + geometry reference, but env-guarded its writer. Provenance says this honestly.
- **Fix the render at boot-time preload, not per-floor lazy loading.** `MainGameScene` bakes
  terrain in `create()`, so textures must already be resident; boot preload is the simplest
  correct point. (ADR alternative #3.)
- **Ship the pack `doorSet` PNGs as not-yet-runtime-wired, documented + tracked (#1902)** rather
  than expanding scope into engine door-wiring, which needs its own visual approval. Same
  not-yet-consumed status for `corridorPool` on the current Floor 2 seed.
- Full rationale + 3 rejected alternatives in ADR
  `docs/knowledge/adr/2026-07-24-floor2-terrain-pack-generated-art-render-fix.md` (extends the
  foundational `2026-07-11-47-mask-terrain-packs.md`).

## Retrospective

### Lessons Learned

- A "wired" system can be **completely inert**: the pack had a manifest, a registry entry, and a
  renderer that reads it — but the one preload call was dead code, so it rendered zero tiles while
  every artifact *looked* present. The only way this surfaced was **observing render counts in the
  real scene** (main-scene-probe-lab), not reading the diff. This is the same class as the
  `spawnerSystem` inert-ship bug (ADR 0034→0036). Trust render counts / real artifacts over "the
  wiring looks right."
- **Test the committed artifact, not just the builder.** Every prior terrain-pack test validated
  the in-memory procedural builder; the runtime actually imports the committed manifest. Those are
  two different truths that legitimately diverge (provenance). The new committed-pack test closes
  that gap and doubles as the durable crenellation-geometry guard (188/188 edge-compat).
- The authored edge-compatibility check at `minEdgePassRate: 1.0` is a **cheap, durable geometry
  proof**: a crenellated/mis-edged silhouette cannot classify all 4×47 cardinal edges, so it fails
  loudly. Prefer this over file-mtime or eyeballing.

### Mistakes Made

- Initially reached for a file **mtime** as "proof" the crenellation fix was in the shipped atlas —
  the adversarial plan review correctly called this out as no proof at all. Early signal: if you
  can't state the *geometric invariant* a check enforces, it isn't a proof. Replaced with the
  188/188 authored edge-compat assertion.
- Spent effort trying to rewrite the session `plan.md` via `filesystem-write_file` (MCP) which
  cannot write outside its allowed root (the session-state dir). Use the native `edit` tool or
  powershell for session-state files.
- Assumed the branch was "at main HEAD, 0 ahead" from an earlier note; `origin/main` had actually
  moved 10 commits. Always re-check `git rev-list --left-right --count origin/main...HEAD` before
  reasoning about merge/diff base.

### Opportunities for Future Improvement

- The two-manifests-two-truths setup (procedural builder output vs committed authored manifest) is
  a maintenance footgun even with the env-guard + committed-pack test. A future session could
  collapse them (e.g. a reproducible in-repo material source) — ADR alternative #2.
- Consider a generic "pack renders N>0 tiles on its assigned floor" headless assertion so any
  future terrain pack can't ship inert the way this one did — a deterministic gate stronger than
  the per-scene probe lab.
- The `gen/` harness being untracked means art regeneration isn't a one-command repo operation.
  If generated packs become common, a sanctioned (network-gated, non-CI) generation entrypoint
  under `scripts/sprites/` would be worth the review cost.
